title: One Without Reincarnation
text: “If your death falls outside the world’s expected course, you’ll truly die for good. That’s a turn of events that would trouble the world itself, you see. The spirit had various reasons for stepping in to save you.”

“And here’s the thing - you’re one of the pillars of the world you originally came from. You’re essentially on loan, summoned into this world. Once your lifespan runs out, you’ll return to your original world. At that point, you’ll forget everything about this world and go back to turning that world’s wheel.”

“Sounds like your name might even change. I wonder what name you’ll carry next time, Motoyasu-kun? Mind you, this isn’t reincarnation, exactly - looks like you’ll carry a few scraps of memory over with you.”
“One morning, knowing nothing at all, you might be a middle schooler, or maybe a high schooler. Fated to turn the world through love, within some allotted span of time.”

Ugh… what was that? Some kind of hellish world? So that meant a world without Filolial-sama, without Filo-tan, without Father - where I’d forget everything and spend eternity romancing pigs, forever!? That would be someone else entirely, not me - and yet apparently it was my future. I refuse, I say!
“That’s how it was with the world I dropped by, yeah. Not long after I left, it got rewound. A world eternally stuck somewhere around the 20th century.”

Hou-kun just declared something unbelievable. Did that mean there was no mistake about it!? That was a truth about my own world I never wanted to know. No wonder - now that I thought back on it since coming here, school had felt strangely long. And apparently, from what I’d heard from Father and the others, I’d moved house far less often than most people too.
“Absolutely not! I refuse to go back to a place like that! Spirit of the spear, please, I’m begging you - don’t send me back to a world like that!”
Here, I made my plea to the spear that granted wishes. I had been holding this particular wish in reserve, but now I made it in earnest.
“Even so, that’s something tied to your very soul.”

“I already sensed you’d wish to refuse - that’s exactly why we’re having this talk. Honestly, setting Naofumi-kun’s situation aside, I’d meant to bring this up with you before we set out. Tonight, actually. Though I never imagined it would come to this.”

Oh, so Ark and Hou-kun were doing this for my sake. I absolutely refused to spend my days back in my original world tiptoeing around some pig’s moods. No thank you to people who’d sulk over a single choice! Where had all our past friendship gone!? Those people were selfish. Rotten reincarnators, every one of them, I say!
“That said, if you truly find this unbearable, or decide you’d rather stop, that choice is yours to make.”
“What does that mean?”
“Exactly what it sounds like. You could give up on Naofumi-kun, and on Filo-chan too, any time you like.”
Somehow, this conversation between Ark and Hou-kun had parts that were terribly hard to follow.
“I refuse to give up!”

“Figured as much, Motoyasu-kun. I’ll say this knowing full well it’ll make you angry, and knowing you’ll probably end up hating me for it - but when it comes to Naofumi-kun specifically, I think he matters least of all, out of everyone.”
What did he just say!?
“What do you mean, Father doesn’t matter!? Father is a supreme being, on par with Filo-tan!”
Now Ark had gone and said something outrageous. Was that it, then? Was he troubled at being told he resembled a Father who didn’t matter at all, or something along those lines?
“Wow, getting called out that bluntly - how does that feel, huh?”
“Yes, yes, I know. What I mean by ‘doesn’t matter, in a sense’ is this, Motoyasu-kun - it’s exactly the same as your own order of priorities.”

My order of priorities? Was this the difference between me and the reincarnators they’d mentioned earlier? Reincarnators put themselves first, they’d said, while I lived for someone else’s sake. So then…? They just kept dodging the question, indeed.
“Sounds like you’re planning something, but I won’t allow it! Father is Father, no matter what!”
I didn’t quite follow, but was this about controlling Father like a puppet or something of that sort?
“Set Father free, I say.”
“Not this again,” the Father of this world would probably say to that - but I couldn’t back down.
“Yeah. That’s exactly why I came.”
Ark said this with a smile. That took the wind right out of my sails. So he actually meant to set Father free?
“…In a way similar to what awaits you when you return to your original world, Naofumi-kun too… has no reincarnation.”
Father had no reincarnation either?

“And that makes freeing him difficult. I don’t want to make Raphtalia-chan grieve the way that girl once did. Ending things after such a painfully brief spell of happiness… I want that happy dream to go on forever, if at all possible. Precisely because nothing truly lasts forever.”
Suddenly I recalled the prophetic inscription. And at the same moment, I remembered - Ark had been telling me about the demon girl who’d carved that very inscription.
“There’s less time than you imagine. The end draws near, without question.”

A being formed from gathered rage… of wrath… At that moment, the orb woven from feathers that Hou-kun had crafted - the one he’d been sprinkling over Filo-tan - was drawn into my spear. The spear burst with light, and a new spear was unlocked.

True Minute Hand of the Dragon Hourglass 0/300 LR — Ability Unlocked… Equipment Bonus, Abilities: “Time Regression,” “Selective Regression,” “Random Regression” — Unique Effect: Parallel Branching Worlds
This was… a new Minute Hand of the Dragon Hourglass!

“Motoyasu-kun, when your lifespan or death draws near, a new parallel world will be born from the information recorded in your spear, and you’ll go on turning the wheel there. Call it a new world if you like, or call it another world overlapping this one.”
“Us… well, not cats, right. The reason the rest of us and Motoyasu-kun were in that world felt like a point of contact with that very trait.”
Hou-kun said this, picking up right where Ark left off. “The rest of us”? Could it be that Hou-kun wasn’t alone in this?
“Honestly, the bird really doesn’t count me among the number, does it.”
“No need to count you in. Either way, things begin and things end… so all you have to do is begin again.”

I didn’t fully grasp Hou-kun’s circumstances, but… I see - begin, end, then begin again. Indeed, I had turned that wheel - looped - countless times before. Much of what these two were saying still escaped me, but if there was meaning in my turning something, then I would turn it endlessly, I say, for Father’s sake, for Big Sister’s, for Filo-tan’s!
“I’ll grant your wish not to be sent back to your original world. Bird, I’ll leave the finishing touches to you.”
“Got it.”

“By wandering through those worlds, the existence known as Naofumi-kun will become firmly established… becoming a source of strength for the Naofumi-kun you hold so dear. And through your looping, Filo-chan’s causality will bind together too, becoming strength of its own.”
“Truly killing two birds with one stone. Brilliant plan.”
“Seriously, cut it out with the teasing already… you’re much better suited playing straight man to Motoyasu-kun’s antics. Honestly.”
“Heh heh heh. Well, playing straight man to Motoyasu-kun is about to come to an end too, soon enough.”

In other words, eventually I would loop, and with each loop, I would become a source of strength for Father. And for Filo-tan too… meaning that by looping, I would be able to stay together with Filo-tan.

“But the Naofumi-kun living in this world must never sense any of it. He must never be made aware. He must never be made to remember. Any of that would shatter the dream, and Raphtalia-chan, Filo-chan… everyone would grieve. Because whatever lies beyond that point wouldn’t be the Naofumi-kun you all know.”
“Yes - this whole time, the only reason I came was to keep Raphtalia-chan from ever being sad,” Ark said, working a spell over me as he spoke.

“You see… I don’t possess anything you could call a soul. I’ve been called ‘a will without substance’ before. That’s why, even standing right here, I feel as though I’m not truly present. Magic and plenty of other things can’t even target me properly - aim carelessly, and I’d simply vanish into the void.”
Ark spoke of himself with a wry, bitter smile.
“Kind of like a living black hole, huh!”
“Don’t joke around either, bird. Besides, that gives the wrong impression - though, well… I won’t deny there’s something ambiguous about it.”
Ark and Hou-kun’s banter sounded like they got along splendidly, which was rather nice to see, I say.
“I can’t even sleep - I only drift into hazy daydreams now and then. In the past, I used to long to be human… actually, when it comes to that, I see quite a lot of you here, Motoyasu-kun.”

Ark gave his necklace a gentle wave, then pressed his hands together before my spear and prayed. Back when Hou-kun had called out to me, and Ark had been muttering to himself alone in the kitchen… could it be that he’d been sensing Father, as some lingering trace of a world already lost…?
